answer: Proof-of-space-time resists sybils: each identity must dedicate a large block of storage AND prove it stayed filled continuously across time, re-challenged at random, so parking idle fakes is not free. A pearl of committed space must be held per identity for the whole duration — a willow bending over a bridge it must keep standing on. One honest agent commits storage once; a swarm needs genuine persistent space per head, and commodity disks cannot be in a thousand places continuously at once.
